info.name: Log Analyzer - Phase 3 (RAG Pipeline)
info.description:
Phase 3 RAG testing collection. Run requests IN ORDER — ingestion first, then queries.

Debugging tips:
- Set breakpoints in LogIngestionService.chunkLogEntries() to watch chunking
- Set breakpoints in RagService.query() to inspect the full RAG pipeline
- Watch the console for embedding model logs and OpenAI request/response logs

item.name: Step 1 — Ingestion
item.description: Ingest logs into the vector store before querying.

item.name: 1a. Ingest — DB errors with stack trace
item.description:
DEBUG HERE: Set breakpoint in LogIngestionService.chunkLogEntries()

Watch how:
- Lines starting with timestamps become separate log entries
- The stack trace (java.sql.SQLException...) stays attached to the ERROR line
- Small entries get grouped into chunks up to 1000 chars

Check the response: how many chunks were created?

item.name: 1d. Ingest — File upload (multipart)
item.description:
Test file upload ingestion. In Postman:
1. Select Body > form-data
2. Key = 'file', Type = File
3. Select any .log or .txt file from your machine

item.name: Step 2 — RAG Queries
item.description:
Query the ingested logs. Run AFTER Step 1.

DEBUG HERE: Set breakpoint in RagService.query() and step through:
1. embeddingModel.embed(question) — watch the question become a vector
2. embeddingStore.findRelevant() — see which chunks match and their scores
3. The prompt string — see how retrieved context is injected
4. chatLanguageModel.generate() — the final LLM call

item.name: 2a. Query — Specific error type (DB errors)
item.description:
WHAT TO OBSERVE:
- relevantChunks: should contain the DB connection error + stack trace
- answer: should be grounded in the actual log content, not hallucinated
- Check console: the OpenAI request log shows the augmented prompt with context

item.name: 2b. Query — Cross-batch retrieval (timeout errors)
item.description:
This question should retrieve chunks from the SECOND ingestion batch (1b).
Tests that the vector store searches across all ingested data.

item.name: 2c. Query — Authentication issues
item.description:
Tests semantic search: the question says 'login' but the logs say 'authentication' and 'session expired'.
Embeddings should match by MEANING, not exact keywords.

item.name: 2d. Query — Broad question (all errors)
item.description:
A broad question should retrieve chunks from MULTIPLE ingestion batches.
Check: does relevantChunks contain errors from both batch 1a and 1b?

item.name: 2e. Query — Unrelated question (tests grounding)
item.description:
CRITICAL TEST: Ask about something NOT in the logs.
The LLM should say it doesn't have enough information.
If it makes up an answer, the RAG grounding prompt isn't working well.

item.name: 2f. Query — Stack trace analysis
item.description:
Tests that stack traces were preserved during chunking.
The answer should reference specific class names and line numbers from the stack trace.

item.name: 2g. Query — System health summary
item.description:
A high-level question. Should pull from healthy logs (batch 1c) AND error logs.
Tests whether RAG can synthesize across different types of log entries.

item.name: Step 3 — Edge Cases
item.description: Test boundary conditions and error scenarios.

item.name: 3a. Query before ingestion (restart server first)
item.description:
Restart the server to clear the in-memory store, then run this.
Tests: what happens when the vector store is empty?
The LLM should indicate no relevant logs were found.

item.name: 3b. Ingest — Single line log
item.description: Minimal input: just one log line. Should produce exactly 1 chunk.

item.name: 3c. Ingest — Large log (many entries)
item.description:
Tests chunking with many entries. Check: chunksIngested should be > 1.
The chunker should split this into multiple chunks of ~1000 chars each.

item.name: 3d. Ingest — Duplicate data
item.description:
Ingest the SAME log as 3b again. The vector store will have duplicates.
Then query for it — does the answer change? Are duplicates in relevantChunks?

item.name: Step 4 — Compare RAG vs Direct Analysis
item.description: Run the SAME log through both Phase 2 (direct LLM) and Phase 3 (RAG) to compare.

item.name: 4a. Phase 2 — Direct EXPLAIN (no RAG)
item.description: Direct LLM analysis — the model uses ONLY the log text you send right now.

item.name: 4b. Phase 3 — RAG query about the same error
item.description:
RAG query — the model gets RETRIEVED CONTEXT from all ingested logs.
Compare this answer with 4a. RAG should provide richer context
(e.g., mentioning the circuit breaker that followed the timeout).
